title: Graviton. Serverless. Apache Iceberg. Your guide to a modern data warehouse strategy
abstract: You need your data warehouse to be fast, open, and accessible to everyone on your team. This session shows you how to get there with Amazon Redshift. Take advantage of Graviton-powered RG instances for faster analytics at lower cost. Eliminate the complexity of managing infrastructure with Redshift Serverless. Query open data formats directly in your data lake with native Apache Iceberg support. And put insights in the hands of every team with natural language access. You'll also learn how multi-warehouse architectures let teams scale independently without duplicating data. Leave with a clear architecture strategy you can apply to your environment.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | White Theater

title: Building real-time applications with event-driven architectures
abstract: Build real-time features using AWS AppSync Events in this hands-on builders' session. Working in small groups with guidance from AWS experts, you'll implement in-app notifications and live updates, configure WebSocket connections, and design data persistence strategies. Using provided code samples, you'll gain practical experience creating responsive, event-driven applications that push updates to connected clients instantly. By the end of this 60-minute session, you'll have working real-time patterns you can apply directly to your own applications. Bring your laptop and come ready to code!
room: Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: AtoZ AI Co-Scientist: Multi-Agent Systems That Do Research With You
abstract: Can an AI system move beyond answering questions to actually conducting research alongside you? We built one. AtoZ AI Co-Scientist is a multi-agent orchestration platform where specialized agents collaborate through a unified interface to discover literature, synthesize knowledge via graph-routed retrieval, generate hypotheses, implement baselines from papers, and run experiments autonomously. In this chalk talk, we dissect the compositional architecture, the graph-routed retrieval system achieving <200ms with structural signals flat search cannot capture, and Co-Scientist Bench—our agent-agnostic evaluation framework. Bring hard questions about reliability, memory, and human oversight.
room: Level 1 | Forum 103

title: Cut token costs by 50%: Building context efficient agents with Strands
abstract: AI agents degrade as conversations exceed context windows. You need retrieval strategies, compression policies, and adaptive storage backends. This code talk covers the three-tier context cache hierarchy of AWS's open source Strands Agents SDK. We'll discuss context management as composable primitives with extension points for custom backends, compression, and retrieval. We'll explore trade-offs between framework and agent-controlled context, how plugins compose without coupling, and where abstractions break under extreme workloads. For developers building or extending agent frameworks.
room: Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Agentic AI Jam - brought to you by Nvidia
abstract: Come with your team of four or join a team and meet new friends in the session. Are you ready to build and deploy agentic AI solutions on AWS? We provide hands-on environments where you can architect intelligent and production-ready agents. How do you orchestrate multi-step agent reasoning with tool use? How can you design agents that plan, act, and self-correct autonomously? Whether you are new to AWS or a seasoned Cloud Ninja, this Jam is your chance to demonstrate your skills and learn new ones. Structured for all experience levels, our sessions include guided exercises, helpful clues, and support from AWS experts to accelerate your agentic AI expertise. Team up, compete with others, climb the leaderboard, and win prizes based on speed and accuracy. With expert guidance every step of the way, all you need is a computer, a desire to learn, and a competitive spirit.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Palace Ballroom I

title: Composing the right orchestration for serverless workflows
abstract: Both AWS Lambda durable functions and AWS Step Functions handle retries, long-running execution, and failure recovery - so how do you choose? In this session, we cut through the confusion with a clear decision framework across three scenarios: human-in-the-loop approvals, long-running AI agent workflows, and multi-service sagas. We'll also show a hybrid pattern where Durable Functions handle inner business logic while Step Functions orchestrate at the macro level - code-level flexibility inside, visual observability outside. Leave with a practical framework and a real production example to guide your next serverless workflow decision.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Data governance for trustworthy AI: from raw data to trusted products
abstract: In this hands-on workshop, transform fictional retailer RetailMax's raw, ungoverned data into trusted, governed data products using Amazon SageMaker platform . Learn to build a business glossary and metadata forms, create an analysis-ready dataset with an ETL job, and trace end-to-end data lineage. Gain hands-on experience enforcing data quality rules, enriching and publishing a governed data product, and sharing it through a publish-and-subscribe model with approval workflows and least-privilege access. Discover how to deliver trustworthy, explainable answers with the Gen-AI data agent. Leave equipped to build the governance and metadata foundation that makes data — and the AI that runs on it — trustworthy across your organization. You must bring your laptop to participate.
room: Level 1 | Grand 122

title: Build AI-Powered Contact Center Agents with Amazon Connect
abstract: Customer-facing AI Agents can resolve issues end-to-end. In this bootcamp, build two complementary AI agents on Amazon Connect AI Customer. First, create an agent-assistance copilot that watches live chats and surfaces real-time knowledge base answers and customer data lookups to human agents. Then build a self-service AI agent that handles routine customer requests autonomously, using MCP tools for Cases and Customer Profiles, and structured escalation paths that preserve full conversation context when a human is needed.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Augustus Ballroom I

title: AWS Escape Room: Exam Prep for AWS Certified AI Practitioner
abstract: Prepare for AWS Certified AI Practitioner by playing this 3D virtual escape room game where Certification prep meets competitive gaming. Generative AI knowledge unlocks doors here. Enter a narrative-driven 3D world, choose your avatar, and tackle progressively harder puzzles tied to AWS Certified AI Practitioner exam domains. Each locked room blends exam-style questions with hands-on labs covering foundation models, responsible AI, prompt engineering, and agentic workflows. Collaborate with teammates, solve challenges under time pressure, and race to escape before your peers to top the leaderboard.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Emperors Ballroom II

title: Automate Penetration Tests with AWS Security Agent
abstract: Security testing shouldn't require weeks of manual effort anymore. In this hands-on lab, configure and execute automated penetration tests using AWS Security Agent. Set up an Agent Space with VPC networking, verify target domains, scope tests by risk type, and monitor execution in real time. Analyze findings with CVSS scores and reproduction steps, then generate actionable reports for your development teams.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Palace Ballroom II

title: What's new in Amazon SageMaker platform
abstract: Amazon SageMaker platform is where data engineering, analytics, and AI  come together. In this session, see what's new across the platform including  innovations in lakehouse architecture that eliminates silos between data  teams and AI teams, catalog capabilities for data discovery and governance,  and streamlined development experiences that get you from raw data to  production models faster. Whether you are building pipelines, running SQL  analytics, or training models, learn how SageMaker platform delivers  enterprise-grade governance with the flexibility to work the way your team  needs.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Accelerate analytics and AI with an open lakehouse architecture on Apache Iceberg
abstract: Stop choosing between your data lake and data warehouse.  Join this session to explore how to build a  unified, open, and secure data lakehouse architecture, on Apache Iceberg. Learn how the lakehouse breaks down data  silos and opens your data estate offering flexibility to use your preferred  query engines and tools that accelerate time to insights. Learn about recent  launches that improve data interoperability and performance, and enable large  language models (LLMs) and AI agents to interact with your data. Discover  robust security features, including consistent fine-grained access controls, attribute-based access control, and tag-based access control that help  democratize data without compromises.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: What's new in Amazon Redshift
abstract: Cut costs, query faster, and unify your warehouse and data lake without trade-offs. In this session, learn how new Graviton-powered RG instances deliver better price-performance, a built-in data lake engine lets you read and write Apache Iceberg tables in place, multi-warehouse architecture gives teams independent scale with shared data, and Redshift Serverless improvements let you get insights on your data without managing infrastructure. Whether you're consolidating on open table formats or building the analytics backbone for AI agents, walk away knowing exactly how to put these capabilities to work.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Powering your agentic AI experience with AWS streaming and messaging
abstract: Organizations are  accelerating innovation with generative and agentic AI—and getting there  depends on a handful of real-time data primitives: durable, high-throughput  ingestion; stream processing and enrichment; low-latency, event-driven  delivery; and a scalable place to land and serve data. In this session, learn  how these primitives come together to power the real-time patterns behind  agentic AI—and where each one fits: streaming into a real-time semantic layer  for fresh retrieval context, event-driven agent invocation so agents act the  instant something happens, and continuously sourcing agentic data stores with  live data. We'll show how to satisfy each primitive—spanning multi-Region  resilience, seamless migration off self-managed infrastructure, direct  landing into open table formats and object storage, and simplified networking
room: Level 3 | Premier 318
services: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK)

title: Human search to agent retrieval: Rearchitecting with OpenSearch Service
abstract: Agents don't search like humans. They fire hundreds of sub-queries per task, maintain stateful memory across sessions, and demand, verified answers before taking action. Traditional search architectures weren't built for this, and at agent scale, latency budgets compress, relevance requirements compound, and retrieval failures cascade into hallucinated outputs. In this session, we walk you through how the shift from human search to agent retrieval is reshaping infrastructure requirements and how the latest capabilities in Amazon OpenSearch Service help you address these unique challenges. You'll leave with a clear understanding of what's changing, why it matters, and how to get started.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Open for Business: OpenAI on AWS
abstract: There is more than one way to put OpenAI to work on AWS, from coding agents that ship production code to knowledge workflows and custom agents. This session tours OpenAI on AWS, starting with the latest OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock. Put them to work through two agentic surfaces: Codex for coding and ChatGPT Work for knowledge work. Then explore Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents powered by OpenAI, for deploying OpenAI-powered agents in your AWS environment. Leave with a map of OpenAI on AWS and when to choose each path.
room: Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: What happens in Bedrock stays in Bedrock
abstract: You want to ship AI, but your compliance team won't sign off until the solution meets their regulatory requirements. This session shows how Bedrock protects data from the hardware up, with zero operator access enforced at the chip so no one, not even AWS operators, can access your prompts and completions. See how data residency controls and strict workload separation extend that protection, and how those guarantees map to the compliance frameworks your teams already use. You leave ready to have the conversation that gets your AI workload approved.
room: Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: How FSI brands are navigating conversational AI for customer engagement
abstract: Financial services customers expect fast, personalized service but compliance, security, and regulatory requirements make automation a high-stakes challenge. Discover how Amazon Connect Customer enables financial institutions to deploy agentic AI self-service that blends autonomous reasoning with deterministic guardrails for identity verification, fraud checks, and regulatory disclosures. Learn how to automate complex interactions like account servicing, disputes, and payments while maintaining full compliance and governance. See how leading institutions are going live in weeks, reducing call volumes, improving containment, and elevating CSAT without compromising trust.
room: Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: One AI Assistant, Every Data Source: Unifying Access with Amazon Quick
abstract: Your data lives in one platform. Your reports live in another. Your documents live somewhere else. Every time someone needs an answer, they spend time figuring out where to look before they can act. Decisions slow down. Teams duplicate work because they cannot find what already exists. New employees take months to become productive because institutional knowledge is trapped in systems they do not know how to navigate. Hear from a customer who solved this by giving their team a single AI assistant that connects across all their enterprise systems. Instead of training people on where to find information, they ask Amazon Quick and get answers grounded in their real business data, regardless of where it lives. Learn how they configured the integration, how their teams adopted it, and what changed about the speed and quality of decision-making across the organization.
room: Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Unexpected resilience: Lessons from a thousand incidents
abstract: After years of investigating incidents - both within AWS and across customer industries - some resilience lessons stand out. Not the obvious ones, but surprises no runbook could anticipate. We share the strangest, most counterintuitive findings from years of troubleshooting under pressure: failure modes nobody planned for, fixes that made things worse, and patterns that only emerge after enough failures. This isn't a best-practices talk - it's a field guide to building resilience from the unexpected. You'll leave with a sharper eye for hidden risks in your infrastructure - and fresh leads on things you didn't know were there.
room: Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: AWS AI Factories: Bring production scale AI to your data center
abstract: Data sovereignty, data gravity, and latency requirements prevent many organizations from running all AI workloads in the public cloud. AWS AI Factories bring AWS and NVIDIA AI infrastructure directly into your data center, fully operated, maintained, and continuously updated by AWS. Run leading foundation models on premises for training and inference without building and managing AI infrastructure yourself or negotiating separate agreements with model providers. In this session, learn how organizations are accelerating AI adoption, reducing time to value, and maintaining full control of their data while benefiting from the AWS experience in their own facilities.
room: Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Inside AWS Trainium3: Hardware innovations for better AI economics
abstract: What does it take to build a chip purpose-made for AI? In this deep dive, we explore Trainium3 architecture innovations: NeuronCore innovations that delivers higher TFLOPs, hardware-accelerated quantization, softmax acceleration, near-memory compute and Mixture-of-Experts optimizations. We'll share micro-benchmark data showing how these choices translate to real performance for Mixture-of-Experts and other demanding workloads. At the system level, we examine the Trn3 UltraServer family, scaling from 32 to 144 chips via NeuronLink fabric to enables up to 4.4x more performance. Leave with a deep understanding of how to evaluate and leverage purpose-built AI Chips for your AI workloads.
room: Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Automate AI governance and risk management
abstract: Governance frameworks designed for static deployments struggle to keep pace with AI systems that learn, adapt, and act autonomously. In this session, walk through AWS Responsible AI best practices for governing AI across the full development lifecycle. Then see how AI Risk Intelligence (AIRI) puts these principles into practice, automating risk management with static checks that verify controls at the code and documentation level and dynamic checks that analyze APIs and traces in real time, giving you continuous visibility into AI risk posture as systems evolve. Learn what it takes to move from periodic manual assessments to continuous, automated governance.
room: Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: From AI Skeptic to Enterprise AI Champion with Amazon Quick
abstract: You deployed an AI assistant. Your team tried it for a week and stopped. The tool could not access the systems where real work happens, gave generic answers because it was disconnected from your enterprise context, and security would not approve broader rollout because the governance story was unclear. That is where most AI deployments stall. Hear from a customer who lived that exact cycle: low adoption, frustrated leadership, and a growing sense that the investment was wasted. They evaluated multiple alternatives and made the switch to Amazon Quick, an AI assistant with governed access to enterprise data, native connectors to the systems their teams already use, and agentic workflows that span business units. Learn what broke in their first deployment, what they looked for in a replacement, and how governed data access turned single-digit adoption into organization-wide usage.
room: Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: From AI Tasks to Autonomous Multi-Agent Workflows with Amazon Quick
abstract: The workflows that matter most in financial services span multiple systems, require multiple types of expertise, and today rely on people as the coordination layer. One person pulls data, another reviews it for compliance, a third routes it for approval. That coordination tax is where your team's time disappears. Amazon Quick changes that equation. Instead of one AI assistant doing one task, specialized agents each handle their piece and hand off to the next automatically. The human stays in the loop for judgment calls, not for data gathering and routing. Hear from a customer who moved from standalone AI use cases to compound, multi-agent workflows with Amazon Quick. Learn how they identified which workflows to orchestrate first, how they designed agent handoffs that satisfy compliance, and what it means now that the coordination layer runs autonomously.
room: Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Rethinking the boundary between messaging and streaming
abstract: Modern event-driven architectures still separate cleanly into "queues" and "streams," but real workloads no longer do. Replay, request-response, ordering, and high throughput increasingly appear across both patterns, making the wrong service choice costly to unwind. This session explores the architectural spectrum across messaging and streaming systems, drawing on services such as Amazon SQS, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon MSK. Through a real CQRS architecture, we build a practical decision framework for when to choose messaging, streaming, or a hybrid approach, and which trade-offs matter most.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Your regulator set your RTO. Not your architecture.
abstract: Organizations with pre-approved failover regions recover in hours. Those without recover in weeks. Same impairment. Same services. One governance decision separates them, and it’s made years before the event. This session presents architectural patterns for multi-Region recovery under sovereignty constraints, drawn from real operational experience with regulated workloads under regional pressure. Three categories: decisions that set your resilience ceiling before any event, dependencies that create circular failure during recovery, and assets nobody backs up until they become the critical path. You leave with the decisions to evaluate before your next DR test.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | White Theater

title: Architecting for non-deterministic components
abstract: Our systems used to behave the same way every time. Now we give them judgment and agency, so they decide and act on their own, and the same inputs can produce different outcomes. Designing reliable architectures around that non-determinism comes down to three questions: where to enforce determinism around the model, when to verify behavior through automated evaluation and reasoning versus human judgment, and how to adapt the patterns (event flows, orchestration, automation) for components that don’t behave predictably. This session presents the design patterns for building systems that decide and act, while preserving the reliability your architecture depends on.
room: Wynn/Encore | Level 1 | Encore Ballroom 5

title: What SOA taught us about building agents in production
abstract: You’ve taken AI agents from prototype to production, and now you own the hard parts: orchestration sprawl, brittle integrations, and behavior hard to test or observe. The patterns that hold up in production look a lot like ones SOA builders already know. This session explores what emerged: multi-agent orchestration mirroring service meshes, tool-use protocols (MCP) formalizing what APIs did for services, evaluation frameworks echoing contract testing, and hard-won lessons about agent observability and trust boundaries. You leave with concrete patterns from the SOA playbook, updated for the agentic era.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: From Pilot to Enterprise Scale with Amazon Quick
abstract: Your AI pilot proved value with a small team. Now you need to deploy across the organization without a dedicated rollout team and without losing what made it work. Hear from a customer who scaled Amazon Quick from an initial deployment to thousands of users across their enterprise. Learn the phased strategy they used to expand Quick's capabilities: connecting teams to enterprise data, automating repetitive workflows, and rolling out agentic features that kept usage growing after the initial adoption wave. Discover what metrics justified continued investment and the operational model they built so scaling Quick did not create a support burden for IT. Walk away with a repeatable framework for taking Amazon Quick from proof-of-concept to production deployment across your organization.
room: Wynn/Encore | Level 1 | Encore Ballroom 5

title: Improving operations with agentic AI
abstract: Your operational telemetry is growing faster than your team. Learn how agentic AI can work across your observability stack, correlating metrics, logs, and traces to detect issues, identify root cause, and initiate remediation without waiting for a human to connect the dots. Explore patterns for agents that triage alerts, reduce noise, surface actionable insights, and execute operational runbooks. See how to integrate agents into your monitoring and incident response workflows, from signal detection through resolution. Leave with practical approaches to reduce mean time to recovery, eliminate repetitive toil, and give your team time to focus on reliability improvements that matter.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Build scalable streaming and messaging applications with Amazon Kinesis and AmazonMSK
abstract: Messaging  and streaming should be simple, elastic, and cost-efficient, no matter how  your workloads change. In this session, discover how Amazon MSK and Amazon  Kinesis Data Streams is making it easier and more affordable to build messaging  and streaming applications at any scale. Learn how you can stop worrying  about capacity planning and reduce costs automatically as your traffic scales  up and down. See how you can land your streaming data directly into Amazon S3  and S3 Tables without building or managing separate pipelines so you can  focus on deriving insights instead of maintaining infrastructure. Join us to  see how these innovations come together to help you move faster, spend less,  and eliminate operational overhead at any scale.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater
services: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK)

title: Accelerating data analytics on Apache Iceberg with Amazon S3 Tables
abstract: Every analytics query starts with how your data is stored. In this session, learn how Amazon S3 Tables deliver purpose-built Iceberg table storage that accelerates query performance, reduces storage costs, and eliminates table maintenance overhead. See how to pair S3 Tables with Athena, Redshift, and EMR to get faster results at lower cost, automate compaction and snapshot management, and simplify your lakehouse without changing your query engine or workflow.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Explore agentic data engineering in Amazon SageMaker
abstract: Data engineering teams lose time to siloed data, manual ETL, and tribal knowledge. This session shows how agents change that in Amazon SageMaker. Use SageMaker Data Agent to trace errors, refactor code, and deploy pipelines in natural language, then bring your own agents through MCP servers to work with third-party clients and models directly on your data. See how the same agentic approach extends across SageMaker, so teams can consolidate fragmented pipelines, standardize environments, and put agents to work on more of the data engineering lifecycle.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Your data, your engine: How open source and open standards power analytics on AWS
abstract: Open table formats and open-source engines like DuckDB give organizations the freedom to choose the right tool for each workload, from interactive dashboards and exploratory analytics to large-scale data processing, with no lock-in. In this session, learn how to capitalize these open tools to build on AWS and turn it into a competitive advantage for your business. We deep dive into the application of each engine, how they complement one another across the analytics lifecycle, and how data governance capabilities like catalog access, fine-grained governance, and consistent table management on AWS further simplify multi-engine architectures in production.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Cut your data lake and lakehouse bills: Cost and performance tuning best practices
abstract: Open data lakehouses and data lakes can quietly accumulate cost through uncompacted small files, over-partitioned tables, and inefficient scan patterns. In this session, learn advanced cost savings and tuning techniques on AWS that cut storage and compute costs while improving performance. We cover partitioning strategies, predicate pushdown optimizations, compaction tradeoffs, graviton efficiencies, intelligent-tiering storage and how to eliminate common anti-patterns that inflate your bill. Learn from practical examples of real-world workloads on Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, Amazon EMR and leave with a comprehensive playbook to lower you analytics costs.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Optimize AI costs with practical deployment blueprints for analytics on AWS
abstract: Delivering AI at enterprise scale demands more than great models — it requires a data and analytics foundation engineered for cost efficiency from day one. This session examines proven deployment blueprints that pair AWS analytics services with AI/ML workloads to maximize price-performance. We explore patterns including right-sizing your analytics infrastructure for training data preparation, on-demand feature extraction, auto-scaling continuous ETL pipelines and selecting optimal storage formats to minimize costs. Through detailed architectural walkthroughs, you'll learn how to instrument cost observability across your analytics stack, apply tagging strategies for AI workload attribution, and implement governance guardrails that prevent runaway spend — turning your data platform into a competitive advantage for AI delivery.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: AWS Glue Data Catalog: Govern data and AI agents with lineage and business context
abstract: AI agents generate SQL, surface insights, and take action on your data. Without governance guardrails, they hallucinate column meanings, query stale tables, and return wrong answers with high confidence. In this session, learn how to ground your AI agents in trusted metadata using AWS Glue Data Catalog. See how to flow business context like glossary terms, descriptions, and quality scores into agent workflows so they generate accurate, schema-aware queries instead of guessing. Walk away with practical patterns for governing AI-assisted analytics the same way you govern human analysts

title: Stop Rolling Back AI Agents: Production Patterns That Work
abstract: The demo shipped. The agent went live. Then someone pulled it back. 74% of enterprises have rolled back a deployed AI agent, and the organizations that invested in governance roll back more often, not less. 88% of pilots never reach production. The infrastructure that gets an agent from demo to production is where the gap lives. We'll walk through the failure patterns that cause rollbacks: agents that fail silently, prompts treated as safety boundaries, and monitoring blind to non-deterministic failures. You'll leave with the patterns that prevent them: infrastructure-level guardrails, blast radius containment, and observability built for probabilistic systems.

title: Lights, Camera, Fargate—A Reality-TV Startup Hardened for Scale on AWS
abstract: In six weeks on reality TV coding show The Full Stack, we built DataSwarm — a data-observability solution shipped as an open-source CLI with cloud-hosted data analysis and remediation. Great demo, wrong architecture. When real users arrived, the demo cracked. So we pivoted. Long-running agents moved off Lambda onto ephemeral ECS Fargate tasks. API keys swapped for firewalled Amazon Bedrock, feature-branched CI/CD with dev-to-prod promotion, and Next.js behind CloudFront, S3, and Lambda@Edge. We break down each tradeoff from first idea to first customer. Leave knowing how to tell demo-grade architectures from customer-grade ones — and when to make the jump.

title: Multicloud Operating Models for ISVs
abstract: ISVs adopting multiple clouds face the same trade-offs. This breakout distills cloud-agnostic operating-model patterns from production multi-cloud estates -- workload placement, abstraction layers, resiliency, and FinOps (optimization, tokenization), and unified observability -- illustrated by SAP running at 25,000+ accounts across AWS, Azure, and GCP. SAP's team walks through what stayed cloud-specific, what they unified, and what they had to invent. Leave with operating-model patterns you can apply across clouds.

title: Network firewall deployment without the guesswork: codify, deploy, done
abstract: Level up your firewall policy operations at scale in this hands-on workshop. Learn to integrate AWS Network Firewall into an existing AWS environment using Terraform. Starting with a realistic multi-VPC setup with AWS Transit Gateway, you will deploy Network Firewall and configure routing, inspection, and logging in minutes using reusable modules. You will then implement the latest Network Firewall features such as web category filtering, JA4 fingerprinting, and EventBridge automation. By the end of this session you will have both practical experience adding Network Firewall to existing environments and reusable patterns ready for your own infrastructure.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 5

title: Architect your metadata hub with AWS Glue Data Catalog
abstract: Your metadata is scattered across warehouses, lakes, ML pipelines, and BI tools. In this session, learn how AWS Glue Data Catalog serves as a single metadata hub that connects all your data assets, enforces consistent governance, and makes every table, model, and feature discoverable across engines and teams. See how to register, enrich, and share metadata at scale, enable cross-account discovery, and give AI agents the context they need to query your data accurately.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | White Theater

title: How Novartis is Using AI to Reimagine Clinical Development on AWS
abstract: Developing a new medicine takes 10–15 years and $2.6 billion — and the timeline is getting longer, not shorter. At Novartis, the Global Drug Development organization recognized that incremental optimization of siloed, sequential clinical processes wouldn't be enough. In this session, learn how Novartis is transforming clinical development with AWS by replacing fragmented legacy systems with a unified NextGen Data Platform. You'll also learn how Novartis stood up an Intelligent Decision System that simulates entire trial operations as a computational twin, and pioneering a collaborative Trial Design Studio where biostatisticians, clinical operations, regulatory, and medical teams co-create protocols in real time.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: How Bayer designed 50K proteins on Amazon Bio Discovery
abstract: This chalk talk explores how to architect agentic AI workflows for generative protein design at enterprise scale. Using Bayer's oncology nanobody campaign as the reference implementation, we walk through the technical and scientific decisions behind a pipeline that generated 50,000 candidates and 3,000 prioritized candidates in weeks using Amazon Bio Discovery. Topics include: model orchestration patterns for generative and predictive models, designing scoring functions that encode biological mechanism (not just binding affinity), iterative feedback loops between computation and wet-lab validation, and scaling considerations for enterprise drug discovery programs. Attendees will leave with a reusable architectural blueprint for building agentic biomolecule design workflows on AWS.
room: Wynn/Encore | Level 1 | Chopin 2

title: Accelerating Apache Spark 4.0 workloads with AWS Analytics
abstract: Apache Spark 4.0 is the latest engine upgrade, and AWS is the best place to run it. Learn best practices for building high-performing Spark 4.0 applications using Amazon EMR. Explore what's new, from the ANSI-compliant type system and Variant data type to Spark Connect and Python-first APIs, and how the AWS performance-optimized runtime amplifies these improvements at scale. See how the Spark Troubleshooting and Upgrade agent accelerates migration by automatically identifying deprecated APIs and recommending code fixes, and how AWS Glue and Apache Iceberg integrations simplify pipelines with open table formats.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Operationalize enterprise event routing with Amazon EventBridge
abstract: Scaling event-driven architectures across multiple AWS accounts has long meant managing fragmented buses, cross-account routing complexity, and developer friction. Explore how Amazon EventBridge delivers the scale, reliability, and developer experience that modern event-driven applications demand. It simplifies event routing across accounts and teams. Whether you're consolidating existing event infrastructure or designing a new event-driven platform, you'll leave with a clearer picture of how to reduce operational complexity and ship faster.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Building event-driven architectures in the age of AI agents
abstract: Event-driven architectures have powered serverless applications for a decade. Now AI agents bring non-deterministic producers, multi-step reasoning chains, and agent-to-agent coordination via events. Learn how the patterns you already know, such as queues, events, and retries, evolve when your consumers are autonomous agents rather than just microservices.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Modernize legacy applications into serverless event-driven systems
abstract: Join us to learn how to plan and automate your modernization. We show how to reverse-engineer architecture and dependencies from existing code, then generate a serverless, event-driven target. See how teams move from monoliths to event-driven microservices in weeks, and make their applications agent-ready in the process.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Data mesh at scale: The automation layer, proven at Experian
abstract: Federated data ownership is easy to draw and hard to enforce. Is governance enforced in process, or in the platform? Enforce it in the platform, and the hard part becomes the seam between central policy and self-serve provisioning most teams never build. On Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio we architect that seam: one project per data-domain for blast-radius isolation, contracts that block non-compliant publication, policy that cascades but only tightens, and a reconciler turning Git-committed JSON into infrastructure. Experian runs it across dozens of data domains in regulated financial services, cutting domain onboarding from months to self-serve.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: From chips to applications: How Trainium powers the next AI frontier
abstract: Every AI breakthrough demands innovation across the full stack — chips, servers, software, and the models built on top — each layer making the next faster, cheaper, and more capable. In this session, discover how AWS and frontier AI builders drive full-stack innovation on AWS Trainium to scale post-training and reinforcement learning, serve at high throughput, and bend the cost-per-token curve. Examine real architectural decisions from silicon to application, then look ahead to what's next in Trainium and AWS infrastructure. Leave with understanding of how each layer of innovation compounds and where to place your bets on AI infrastructure.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Build a governed enterprise AI/ML platform on SageMaker AI
abstract: Enterprises struggle with fragmented ML tooling, inconsistent governance, and limited model health visibility. This session demonstrates a unified platform on Amazon SageMaker AI addressing these challenges across regulated industries. We cover multi-account architecture with environment-isolated domains, SageMaker AI Studio and MLflow/Model Registry as the central governance checkpoint with approval workflows, and CI/CD-driven model promotion with validation gates. We extend this to LLM fine-tuning — adapter versioning, evaluation benchmarks, and human-in-the-loop sign-off within the same registry-driven pipeline. Finally, we close the loop with model monitoring for drift, inference logging, and automated alerting. Leave with a reference architecture and decision frameworks.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Data Prep to Deployment: How Tencent Games Scaled to 1,000 GPUs on SageMaker HyperPod
abstract: Join us to see how Amazon SageMaker HyperPod lets teams build complete training pipelines, from data prep and transformations through distributed training to seamless model deployment, all on one resilient, self-healing platform with no re-platforming required. Then, hear how Tencent Games, a game AI team (not an infra team), went from first cluster to thousand-GPU training in weeks for their VISVISE engine powering 90+ titles including PUBG Mobile. Walk away with lessons learned from real production workloads and best practices for EFA networking, FSx storage, and GPU fault tolerance.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Accelerate Domain-Specific AI with Amazon SageMaker AI and Forge
abstract: Forge accelerates AI solution development on AWS. In this session, learn about Forge's capabilities and how to use them to create custom evaluations for your use case, incorporate your data into your AI solution, and select the right model for your needs.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: World Models & Physical AI: The Next Frontier in Intelligent Systems
abstract: World models—AI systems that simulate and predict complex environments—are emerging with new modalities including Video, Vision, Language, Action to power physical AI, autonomous systems, and real-time video generation. From humanoid robotics to immersive entertainment, these models are transforming how machines perceive, think, and interact with the physical world. In this panel, hear from researchers and customers on how they're building and deploying world models in production, the business opportunities they unlock, and the unique technical challenges they present. Learn how AWS AI infrastructure powers these use cases at scale with speed, efficiency, and automatic fault recovery.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Customize open models for accuracy, cost, and latency on SageMaker AI
abstract: An off-the-shelf model may not meet the accuracy, cost, or latency requirements of your specialized business task. Across businesses from retail to financial services, organizations are customizing open-weight models to unlock higher value. In this session, learn how to customize open-weight models with Amazon SageMaker AI, including for domain-specific workflows and agents. Intuit shares how it is using SageMaker AI with features such as serverless model customization and reinforcement learning, on its proprietary data to unlock business value and cut costs.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Automate your business processes with workflow agents on AgentCore
abstract: The agents with the clearest ROI don't wait for a prompt. They wake on an event and run a process to completion. A new lead triggers a prospecting agent, a filed ticket triggers IT resolution, a spend threshold triggers a campaign adjustment. This session covers best practices for building workflow agents on AgentCore: triggering agents from event sources, running long tasks asynchronously on Runtime, connecting to systems of record through gateway, holding state with memory, adding human-in-the-loop approvals, and enforcing actions with policies the agent cannot bypass.
room: Level 1 | Grand 115

title: Trusting agents in production: end-to-end security with AgentCore
abstract: AI agents call APIs, access databases, and act on behalf of users, making security non-negotiable before you go to production. But they introduce new attack surfaces: persistent sessions, autonomous tool execution, and permissions that compound across steps. This session shows how to secure agents end to end with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: microVM isolation so sessions can't leak into each other, identity propagation so every action traces back to a user, Gateway policies that control which tools agents can reach, and Cedar authorization for least-privilege at every call. Leave with a blueprint for production.
room: Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: An insider’s look into architecture choices for Amazon DynamoDB
abstract: To overcome the performance and scale limitations of relational databases, AWS built Amazon DynamoDB to deliver consistent single-digit millisecond performance at any scale for the most demanding applications on the planet. In this session, learn about the architecture choices for Amazon DynamoDB. Gain a better understanding of when to use DynamoDB and why DynamoDB is used by over one million AWS customers, and powers hundreds of applications that exceed half a million requests per second. Leave with a new perspective on how to design your own applications.
room: Level 1 | Grand 119

title: Deep dive into Elastic Load Balancing for modern workloads
abstract: Architect high-performance, resilient network infrastructure using Network Load Balancer and Gateway Load Balancer. This deep dive covers advanced load balancing, multi-protocol support, and security appliance integration at scale. In this session, we explore NLB source IP preservation, GWLB transparent inspection architecture, and deployment patterns. Topics include performance optimization, troubleshooting methodologies, QUIC support, and resilience capabilities including Zonal Shift and Zonal Autoshift. Walk away with practical blueprints for designing architectures that deliver high availability and predictable performance while maintaining inline security inspection and compliance—whether you're running financial trading platforms, gaming backends, or large-scale SaaS.
room: Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater
